Presence.question: How should participants appear while working on the board?
Presence.answer: Participant avatars, named cursors, and colored selection outlines. Cursor names appear on movement or hover to reduce clutter.
options_presented: Participant avatars, named cursors, and colored selection outlines (recommended).
Participant avatars and named cursors; selections visible only to the selecting person.
Participant avatars only.

Presence.question: How should Viewers appear to other participants?
Presence.answer: Include Viewers in the participant list; hide their cursors and selections.
options_presented: Include Viewers in the participant list; hide their cursors and selections (recommended).
Show Viewer cursors and selections with a Viewer label.
Let each Viewer choose whether to share cursor and selections; presence remains visible.

Presence.question: How should presence appear when the same person opens multiple tabs or devices?
Presence.answer: One avatar per person, showing only their most recently active cursor.
options_presented: One avatar per person, separate cursors for active tabs/devices with distinguishing labels (recommended).
One avatar per person, showing only their most recently active cursor.
Separate avatar and cursor for every tab/device.

Presence.question: What should happen when someone becomes inactive or loses connection?
Presence.answer: Inactive: fade idle cursors and avatar. Disconnected: remove disconnected participants immediately upon detection.
options_presented: Fade idle cursors; briefly mark disconnected participants as reconnecting before removing (recommended).
Keep idle cursors visible; remove disconnected participants immediately.
Hide idle cursors; keep disconnected participants listed until they reconnect or board closes.
Presence.notes: User supplied a custom combination; no reconnecting grace display. User then chose to proceed to concurrent changes.

Concurrent changes.question: When two people edit text in the same object, how should it behave?
Concurrent changes.answer: One person edits at a time. Reserve text for whoever starts editing and show others who is editing.
options_presented: Both type simultaneously with live merge and text cursors (recommended).
One person edits at a time with visible reservation.
Simultaneous editing with live merge and a warning.

Concurrent changes.question: While someone edits text, what can others do to the same object?
Concurrent changes.answer: Select it, but wait to modify it. Reserve text, position, size, formatting, and deletion until text editing ends.
options_presented: Select only; wait to modify (recommended).
Move, resize, and style; reserve text and deletion.
Any action except editing text, including deletion.

Concurrent changes.question: When should the editing reservation end?
Concurrent changes.answer: When the editor finishes, leaves the text field, or disconnects. Keep it while connected even when idle.
options_presented: Finish, leave, inactivity with warning, or disconnection (recommended).
Finish, leave, or disconnection; retain while connected and idle.
Finish or leave, with Owner override and disconnection release.

Concurrent changes.question: When two people drag or resize the same object, how should it behave?
Concurrent changes.answer: First person reserves the object until the gesture ends. Apply this same approach to all conflicting actions between users.
options_presented: Reserve for first person until gesture ends; show who is manipulating (recommended).
Allow simultaneous gestures; last accepted position or size wins.
Allow both previews but give first person priority.
Concurrent changes.notes: User explicitly generalized first-action reservation to all conflicting concurrent actions. Follow-up summarized text, dragging, resizing, rotating, formatting, deleting, and structural changes; user chose next area. Group and mind-map reservation granularity remains to be specified during planning or further discussion; no global board lock was requested.

Personal undo.question: If someone changes an object after your edit, how should Undo behave?
Personal undo.answer: Preserve their later change, skip the conflicting undo step, and briefly explain why. Independent changes remain undoable.
options_presented: Preserve later changes and skip conflicting steps with explanation (recommended).
Stop at the conflicting step and offer manual skip.
Offer earlier version as a separate object.

Personal undo.question: How should undo history work across tabs and devices?
Personal undo.answer: Separate history for each tab or device; undo affects changes made in that window.
options_presented: Separate history for each tab or device (recommended).
Shared personal history across tabs and devices.

Personal undo.question: How long should undo history remain available?
Personal undo.answer: Keep eligible history through temporary disconnections; reset when the board is reloaded or closed.
options_presented: Keep through temporary disconnections; reset on reload or close (recommended).
Keep across reloads in the same tab, validating content and permissions.

Personal undo.question: How should changes be grouped into undo steps?
Personal undo.answer: One step per completed editing session. A drag, resize, rotation, or multi-object operation is one step; all text changes before leaving a text field undo together.
options_presented: One step per meaningful action, with typing grouped into short bursts (recommended).
One step per completed editing session; text changes before leaving the field undo together.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: How should pending edits be handled when the shared canvas changed during disconnection?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: With current write permission, notify the user that the canvas changed and offer Load latest or Create a private copy containing the entire local version. Do not merge divergent changes or overwrite the shared canvas.
options_presented: Automatically apply independent edits; review conflicts.
Automatically recover conflicting objects as copies.
Review all pending edits.
Reconnection and permission changes.notes: User rejected merging and initially chose full shared-canvas overwrite. Later explicitly revoked that choice in favor of a separate private fork, then confirmed this applies both to ordinary reconnection and restored write permission. Earlier overwrite and overwrite-race decisions are superseded.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: What should Load latest do with unsaved local work?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: Offer to download the local version as a recovery copy before loading the updated shared canvas. User can download, continue without downloading, or cancel.
options_presented: Keep a downloadable recovery copy then load latest.
Discard after explicit confirmation.
Reconnection and permission changes.notes: User supplied the download offer as a third option.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: What happens if an Editor becomes a Viewer with pending work?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: Switch to read-only, explain the permission change, preserve pending work locally for recovery if write permission returns, and load the latest authorized canvas.
options_presented: Switch to read-only and preserve work until write permission returns (recommended).
Switch to read-only and offer an editable recovery download.
Pause at permission-change screen with return or retry.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: What happens after full access removal?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: Hide the canvas and stop synchronization upon detection. Preserve pending work locally until access is restored. Show access-removal message with return-to-library and check-access actions. Recovery requires current write permission.
options_presented: Preserve pending work locally until access returns (recommended).
Remove local pending work immediately.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: How should preserved work be recovered after write permission returns?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: Ask before recovering it. If the shared canvas is unchanged, offer to restore pending edits. If changed, offer Load latest or Create a private copy.
options_presented: Ask before recovering (recommended).
Automatically recover if unchanged.
Reconnection and permission changes.notes: Final divergent-version choices reflect the later explicit rollback of shared-canvas overwrite.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: What should other participants experience after Keep my version replaces the canvas?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: User revoked the shared-canvas replacement capability entirely. Fork local work into a separate private board owned by the recovering user, or load latest after offering a recovery download.
options_presented: Reload replacement with notice and preserve others pending work.
Pause on Canvas replaced notice.
Reconnection and permission changes.notes: Neither proposed replacement behavior is authorized; the user supplied a revised recovery design.

Reconnection and permission changes.question: Use Load latest or Create a private copy for ordinary disconnection as well as restored write permission?
Reconnection and permission changes.answer: Yes. Apply the same choice in both situations, gated by current write permission.
options_presented: Yes, use both choices in both situations (recommended).
Only offer a fork after permission restoration.
